label: duplicate-logic-use-existing-helper
name: New code re-derives a value, predicate, loop, sequence or helper that already exists in the repository or in the same diff
description: What breaks: two copies drift. A hand-written spin loop duplicates mwaitx::wait_for_not_event (2719158416 'couldn't we use mwaitx::wait_for_not_event for this?'); an inline getenv/device test duplicates fwd_hw_attn_enabled() (3029194687 'the function I just added early this week'); a second getenv of USE_HW_ATTN across the pos/tron layer boundary (3454460758); a pool-worker key computed inline at one site and by stats->pool_worker() at two others (4147010638 'Suggest one helper for all three'); an if/else whose branches are the same stanza except a type name (3405150087); the safety-critical reservation.commit() -> guard.commit() -> tracker.push() sequence copied four times (3907214892 'a future edit that misses one copy becomes a silent staging-lifetime bug'); gof_configure passed 1.0f where the model holds the real pre-attention scalar (2897190682); 1/sqrt(head_size) re-derived while the state constructor handles gemma softcapping (3036995239); a call that re-iterates the list the loop above just filled (4029533521); a push_back loop next to a sibling resize (3102140611, withdrawn after checking the element type). Procedure: for every added predicate, formula, wait loop or sequence grep h/ and src/ (and the base branch since the PR branched) for a function or expression with the same operands; for any value passed as a literal to a configure function find the member that already computes it; for any sequence whose comment says ordering matters count its copies at HEAD; for adjacent loops over one container ask for one loop. Ask form: 'couldn't we use X for this?', 'this should be replaced with X'.
disposition_reason: No existing check searches for an existing helper or a second copy; 10 rows over 10 PRs.
agent_feasibility: yes: grep for same-operand expressions and for the diff's own new helpers; the layering constraint (3454460758) needs the include-layer rule from docs.

members.concern: The new hand-written spin loop that polls an HBM (FPGA high-bandwidth memory) address until it matches the written value duplicates an existing helper, mwaitx::wait_for_not_event (the project's wait-until-memory-changes primitive in h/system/mwaitx.hpp); Wade asks whether that helper could be used for both the V wait and the K wait.

detection.trigger: The diff adds a loop of the form `while (*addr != val) { if (rdtsc() - start >= timeout) break; }` or any busy-wait on a memory word with a timeout.
detection.procedure: grep -rn 'wait_for_not_event\|wait_for_event\|spin_until\|rdtsc' h/system h/pos; read h/system/mwaitx.hpp for the signature and its constraints (volatile uint64_t*, alignment); compare with the added loop's operand type and address arithmetic.
detection.question: Does an existing helper in h/system or h/common already express this wait, and does the added loop differ from it in any way the author can name?

members.quote: couldn't we use mwaitx::wait_for_not_event for this (and the k wait)?
members.note: At head 2d53016b44 h/system/mwaitx.hpp:84-92 declares wait_for_not_event taking a volatile uint64_t* trigger. The added loop reads `*vhbm_addr` where vhbm_addr = base + offset - 6 bytes (V case), which is not 8-byte aligned; the author's reply 'concerned RE alignment' refers to that. Wade's comment was posted 2026-01-23 before the author's reply; the loop stayed hand-written at the approved head (hwattention.hpp:395-520).

members.concern: The hunk gates the hardware-attention path with an ad hoc check (device list non-empty and the TRON_DISABLE_HW_ATTN environment variable unset), and Wade asks to use the existing helper fwd_hw_attn_enabled() that he added to the base branch that week instead.

detection.trigger: The diff adds an inline predicate (a getenv call, a feature-flag read, a device-presence test) at a call site instead of calling a named function.
detection.procedure: For each added getenv("...") or inline flag expression, grep BASE and recent base-branch commits for a function whose body reads the same variable or decides the same question: `git grep -n 'TRON_DISABLE_HW_ATTN\|hw_attn_enabled' BASE -- h src` and `git log -S'<env var>' --since='2 weeks ago' origin/<base>`. If a helper exists, the finding is 'replace with <helper>'; if the PR also introduces a new env var name, compare with the helper's variable name.
detection.question: Does a function at BASE (or on the base branch since the PR branched) already decide this predicate, so that the added inline check is a second, divergent copy?

members.quote: this should be replaced with the `fwd_hw_attn_enabled()` function I just added early this week
members.note: Wade relied on his own base-branch commit from that week (fwd_hw_attn_enabled); the worktree's main history shows the symbol only from 2026-07 commits, so the April base-branch commit is not in this worktree (Insufficient data on its id). The PR's own commit list contains 'use fwd_hw_attn_enabled() instead of new env var.' and head 1a88e897e1 model.hpp:827 reads `if (have_devices && fwd_hw_attn_enabled())`, so the change was applied. Pattern: a reviewer who recently touched the same area checks that the PR did not re-implement what he just added; an agent reproduces this with git log on the base branch since the merge-base.

members.concern: The new bitfile-capability warning in PosDevice::init re-reads the USE_HW_ATTN environment variable instead of calling the one existing reader fwd_hw_attn_enabled() (declared in a tron-layer header that the pos layer must not include); Wade asks for an extern declaration in device.cpp so the getenv logic exists once.

detection.trigger: A hunk adds a getenv (or other config read) for a variable name that another function in the repository already reads and caches, and the two sites sit in different layers so the obvious #include is forbidden.
detection.procedure: grep the diff for std::getenv / getenv names; for each name grep h/ and src/ for other readers; if one exists in a different layer (src/pos vs h/tron), check README.code-org.md or the include graph for the layering rule; propose an extern declaration of the existing function in the .cpp instead of a second parse.
detection.question: Does the repository already have one function that reads and caches this environment variable, and can this file call it without violating the include layering?

members.quote: could we maybe `extern fwd_hw_attn_enabled()` in this file and use that, rather than duplicating the `getenv` read logic? I know including `hw_attn_config.hpp` in this file would break layering, just looking for an alternative.
members.note: Verified at head 39396c8728: src/pos/device.cpp:59 has `extern bool fwd_hw_attn_enabled();` and line 166 calls `tron::fwd_hw_attn_enabled()`; device.cpp does not include hw_attn_config.hpp. The definition moved to a new file src/tron/models/hw_attn_config.cpp (+18). Wade knew the layering rule (pos layer must not include tron headers) from outside the diff. No author reply in the thread; outcome inferred from the head code. Form is a question that carries a concrete suggestion.

members.concern: Nit: the pool-worker row key is computed two ways in the same file (an inline expression tp.num_workers() - n_attn_workers + worker_ix at one site, stats->pool_worker(...) at two others); use one helper at all three so the rows cannot drift if the convention changes.

detection.trigger: The diff introduces a helper that computes a key or index (pool_worker) and also an inline expression with the same formula at another site in the same or a related file.
detection.procedure: Take the helper's body formula (`num_workers - n_attn_workers + ix`) and grep the diff and the file at HEAD for the same operands in an arithmetic expression outside the helper (`grep -n 'num_workers() - n_attn_workers'`). Also grep every call of the helper. Report each site that computes the key without the helper.
detection.question: Is the same row key or index derived by more than one expression, so that a change to the convention at one site would silently desynchronize the others?

members.quote: Here it is the inline `pool_worker_ix` (`tp.num_workers() - n_attn_workers + worker_ix`, line 797), while `run_joins` (line 1343) and `apply_page_range` (line 1485) call `stats->pool_worker(...)`. Suggest one helper for all three
members.note: Verified at 0f784c44ff self_attention.hpp:797 `const size_t pool_worker_ix = tp.num_workers() - n_attn_workers + worker_ix;`, :1343 `stats->pool_worker(worker_ix, n_attn_workers)`, :1485 `stats_ref.pool_worker(scratchpad, n_attn_workers)`. Wade cites all three line numbers, so he read the whole file at the commit. Fixed in the final commit ('one row-key helper').

members.concern: Inside the attention branch of hw_prepare, a new if/else on workreq->attn_req logs the weight command twice with near-identical text; Wade asks to drop the guard and one copy because the ternary already picks the label.

detection.trigger: a diff adds an if/else where both branches contain the same statement text except for one type name or one string literal, or adds a block that repeats an existing block a few lines away
detection.procedure: for each added if/else, diff the two branch bodies token by token; note which tokens differ (here only weights_cmd_attn_fields vs weights_cmd_matmul_fields and a space in the format string); check whether an existing expression in the same statement already encodes the condition (the ternary workreq->attn_req ? "hwattn" : "legacy")
detection.question: Do the two branches differ in anything a reader or the output depends on, and if only by a type name, can one statement with the right type replace both?

members.quote: this stanza is an exact duplicate of the one below... remove the guard and one of the copies? You already have ternary logic to print the right 'type' with `workreq->attn_req ? "hwattn" : "legacy",`
members.note: Verified at 247c8a4c22 src/pos/worker.cpp:1419-1431: the branches differ only by the fields type (weights_cmd_attn_fields vs weights_cmd_matmul_fields) and one space in the format string, so 'exact' was slightly wrong, which the author pointed out ('They're not exact. the fields object is a different type'). The author first pushed back, then the commit 'remove duplicate debug output.' removed one copy: at a62d15a3dc only one 'TX WORKER hw_prepare ... wcmd' log line remains (line 1418). Wade's own follow-up (3405963004) gives the stronger reason: the else is unreachable.

members.concern: The sort/group/dispatch block, which carries the staging-lifetime-critical ordering reservation.commit() -> guard.commit() -> tracker.push(pending_xfer{...}) from PR #3928, now exists in four near-verbatim copies across gof.cpp and model.hpp, with twin request structs and two copies of the run-grouping predicate; a future edit that misses one copy becomes a silent staging-lifetime bug rather than a compile error.

detection.trigger: The diff adds a second (or further) copy of a statement sequence whose order is documented as safety-critical (a comment near one copy explains why the ordering matters), or adds a struct that is another struct plus one member, or repeats a predicate lambda in two files.
detection.procedure: Take the ordered call sequence from the hunk (reservation.commit, guard.commit, tracker.push) and grep each name across h/ and src/; list every site where the three appear in sequence and note which sites keep the explanatory comment. Diff the two request structs field by field. Diff the grouping predicates (same layer, consecutive gof_in_shard, same window, same shard). Check git log / PR history for where the ordering was introduced (here #3928) to confirm it is safety-critical.
detection.question: If someone changes the commit ordering, the grouping predicate or a pending_xfer field in one copy, does the compiler or any test catch the other copies?

members.quote: All four carry the same safety-critical sequence from the staging-lifetime work in #3928: reservation.commit() -> guard.commit() -> tracker.push(pending_xfer{...}), where the ordering is what keeps staging alive under submitted descriptors
members.note: Wade cross-referenced two files and the originating PR #3928 to establish why the ordering is safety-critical, and noted the explanatory comment survives only next to some copies (comment-lost-in-copy). He did not propose the helper's shape; the author did. Head 7f80aa17da evidence: commit 'Consolidate prepared-transfer grouping and dispatch into one helper'; gof.cpp:438 void dispatch_prepared_gof_xfers(std::span<prepared_gof_xfer> ...) called from gof.cpp:557 and model.hpp:3111 - so the four copies became one helper.

members.concern: The call to gof_configure (the function that stores model-level constants for the GOF DMA path) passes a literal 1.0f as the pre-attention scalar, but the model already holds the real scalar (e.g. rsqrt of head size, or the gemma query pre-attention scalar), so the hard-coded value is wrong.

detection.trigger: A diff line passes a numeric literal (1.0f, 0, 128) as an argument to a configure/init function whose parameter name denotes a model- or hardware-derived quantity (scalar, scale, head_size, num_heads).
detection.procedure: For each literal argument, read the callee's parameter name. Grep the enclosing class and its members (here model.hpp, self_attention.hpp) for a field with the same stem (pre_attn_scalar, hw_attn_cfg). If such a field exists and is set from model config, the literal is a placeholder.
detection.question: Does the enclosing object already compute or store the value this literal stands in for, and does that stored value differ from the literal for any supported model?

members.quote: the pre_attn scalar needs to come from the model... 1.0f is not the correct value, currently
members.note: Verified: commit 6d92cc197 replaced 1.0f with self_attn_state.hw_attn_cfg.pre_attn_scalar [h/tron/models/model.hpp:761 at 6d92cc197]. At the commented commit 034b9def5d, model.hpp already referenced pre_attn_scalar at lines 222 and 381, so the correct source was visible in the same file. Wade read beyond the hunk (he knew the model owns the scalar).

members.concern: The new gof_configure_for_model() computes the pre-attention scalar as 1/sqrt(head_size) for every model, but the model state constructor already derives it from the model's query_pre_attn_scalar under softcapping (gemma), so the new code duplicates the formula and diverges from the source of truth.

detection.trigger: A hunk re-derives a per-model value (scalar, size, flag) from a constant or a formula instead of reading it from the place that already computes it for the model.
detection.procedure: Take the computed quantity's name (here rsqrt_pre_attn_scalar / pre_attn_scalar); grep h/ src/ for the existing computation; compare the branches of the existing computation (if constexpr on model traits, config fields) with the new one-line formula; list model types for which they differ.
detection.question: Is there an existing computation of the same quantity with more cases than the new code, and does the new code read it or copy only one branch?

members.quote: the model itself can provide this pre-attn scalar... so assuming it's always `1.0f / sqrtf(static_cast<float>(model_t::head_size)` isn't completely accurate. It should be modeled after this logic found in `state` constructor:
members.note: Verified at d39c222fa8: src/tron/gof_model.cpp:11 'float scalar = 1.0f / sqrtf(static_cast<float>(model_t::head_size));' and h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp:361-374 has the if constexpr (softcapping) branch using enclosing_state.plugin_state.model.query_pre_attn_scalar; h/tron/plugins/llama.hpp:257 declares static_option<is_gemma2, float> query_pre_attn_scalar with default 144.0f. Wade approved one minute later at the same commit without a reply recorded; the digest has no author response. He quotes the alternative code in a fenced block instead of a suggestion block.

members.concern: The new call hw_plan.index_passes_by_job(items) iterates the passes list immediately after a loop at the same site that already iterates passes to move them into hw_plan and call prepare_raw_result per query; Wade asks for one combined loop or utility, suggesting the name set_passes(passes, items).

detection.trigger: A hunk adds a call (or a loop) directly after an existing loop in the same function, and the callee's body iterates the same container (same `.size()` bound or range-for over the same member) that the loop above just filled or walked.
detection.procedure: Read the callee at the same commit (common.hpp:804-822 at af295981ea: `for (size_t pi = 0; pi < passes.size(); ++pi) for (hw_query const& query : pass.queries)`), and the loop above the call site (model.hpp:2651-2657: `for (size_t i = 0; i < passes.size(); ++i) ... for (auto const& query : pass.queries) ... prepare_raw_result(query.job_ix)`). Confirm both walk passes and, inside, pass.queries, and that nothing between them changes passes. Propose a single member that takes the moved vector plus the per-query action (the head's `set_passes(std::vector<hw_pass>, items, prepare_query)` at common.hpp:806 is the adopted form).
detection.question: Do the loop just above the new call and the callee walk the same container with the same inner iteration, with nothing in between that requires the second pass, so that one loop could do both?

members.quote: we have a loop just above that already iterates up to `passes.size()`, and then `index_passes_by_job` turns around and iterates that list again. Can we combine these into a single utility/loop? Maybe something like `set_passes(passes, items)`?
members.note: Verified at af295981ea (the review commit): model.hpp:2651-2657 loops `for (size_t i = 0; i < passes.size(); ++i)` moving each pass into hw_plan.passes[i] and calling prepare_raw_result for every query; then line 2660 calls index_passes_by_job, whose body (common.hpp:804-822) loops `for (size_t pi = 0; pi < passes.size(); ++pi)` and over `pass.queries` again, building by_job. At the merged head c00cd6d6d3 the author adopted the suggestion by name: common.hpp:806 `void set_passes(std::vector<hw_pass> new_passes, ... prepare_query)` which calls `index_passes_by_job(items, prepare_query)` (line 811), and model.hpp:2666 calls `q_batch->hw_plan.set_passes(std::move(passes), q_batch->items, ...)`. This is a per-forward hot-path site (construct_hw_plan runs each forward pass), but Wade framed it as structure ('combine into a single utility'), not as a measured cost. No approval by Wade recorded in the digest.

members.concern: Asks whether the hand-written while/push_back loop that grows hw_v_stars (the per-pass vector of result-buffer rows) could be replaced by a single std::vector::resize call, like the attn_launchers.resize two lines above it.

detection.trigger: A diff adds a hand-written loop that grows or fills a standard container (while size < n push_back(...), for-loop of push_back) next to, or in the same function as, an existing resize/assign call on a sibling container.
detection.procedure: Read the hunk and the container's declaration (grep the member name in the header). Determine the element type and what state the loop puts each new element in. Compare with what resize would produce (value-initialized element: nullptr for unique_ptr, zero for scalars, default ctor for classes). If equal, the loop can be one call; if not (e.g. unique_ptr must be non-null), the loop is needed and the comment must not be posted.
detection.question: Does std::vector::resize produce the same element state that the loop produces, so the loop is redundant?

members.quote: you should be able to use `resize` for this...?
members.note: Code fact at 9d0d649274: hw_v_stars is a vector of std::unique_ptr<v_stars_row_t>; the loop is `while (hw_v_stars.size() < workload.passes.size()) hw_v_stars.push_back(std::make_unique<v_stars_row_t>());` directly after `attn_launchers.resize(...)`. Wade did not check the element type before asking; the author answered 'If you have a cleaner call I'll shift', and Wade then checked and retracted (see 3102275102). Pattern: the question was triggered by the adjacent resize analogy, not by reading the type.

codex_bullets.bullet: Identify who owns each buffer, reference, queue entry, and completion signal from submission through completion, cancellation, and reuse. Check container reallocation and scheduler storage rebuilds while references remain live.
codex_bullets.reason: Four Wade comments across PRs 2499, 2906, 4128 trace buffer and reference lifetime under DMA or reallocation; the Claude skill has no check on asynchronous ownership.

codex_bullets.bullet: Multiply a new operation by its real frequency: per element, token, layer, worker, submission, or polling iteration. Inspect allocation before an empty-queue check, redundant zeroing, repeated gathers, extra passes, and unnecessary sorting.
codex_bullets.reason: Four Wade comments (PRs 4128, 2903, 4258) plus the 2906 paste. The sub-list (memset, six vectors, sort, alloc-before-empty-check) is lifted verbatim from the two PR 4128 inline comments. Generalize the frequency rule; do not copy the 4128 item list.

codex_bullets.bullet: Give one place responsibility for a complete operation record, or prove the split producers stay paired on every call path. Check begin/end, reset, aggregation, and publication together.
codex_bullets.reason: Three comments (PRs 4596, 2287). No Claude check on paired producers or reset.

codex_bullets.bullet: Prefer one implementation of a safety-critical ordering, grouping rule, or index convention when copies can diverge. Use the nearest suitable helper without adding speculative infrastructure.
codex_bullets.reason: Five comments (PRs 4128, 4596, 2980, 1920), plus 4029533521 and the 4007 approval praising "pulling some of the scattered, ad-hoc math into utilities". Frequent theme; no Claude check.

codex_bullets.bullet: Reuse existing configuration accessors and model parameters instead of copying environment reads or deriving a setting from a correlated dimension. Check that the normal wrapper or entry point exposes the feature.
codex_bullets.reason: Five quoted (PRs 3016, 2089, 2426, 2176, 3490); also 3029194687, 3036995239, 2915275194, 3866435051. One of the most frequent themes in the corpus. No Claude check.

codex_bullets.bullet: When several sites repeat an ownership handoff, compare the full ordering and failure cleanup. A helper is useful when it keeps the invariant in one place. Similar spelling alone is not enough reason to refactor.
codex_bullets.reason: Two comments (PRs 4128, 2980). Procedure form of C27; adopt together with C27.
